operations.name: health
operations.db3_reason: Readiness covers the PostgreSQL schema, pg_trgm, and canonical KB tables.

operations.name: embedding_dimension
operations.db3_reason: The effective dimension is canonical PostgreSQL and pgvector schema evidence.

operations.name: pool_status
operations.db3_reason: Connection-pool occupancy and failure counters describe the DB2 PostgreSQL owner.

operations.name: embedding_refusals
operations.db3_reason: Width-refusal evidence diagnoses writes rejected by DB2's canonical pgvector schema.

operations.name: postgres_status
operations.db3_reason: Connection pressure, PostgreSQL recovery role, and WAL replay lag remain DB2 operational evidence.

operations.name: reembed_status
operations.db3_reason: The canonical re-embedding maintenance marker coordinates DB2 schema width and authoritative corpus rebuilds.

operations.name: reembed_clear
operations.db3_reason: Clearing the canonical re-embedding maintenance marker remains a DB2 lifecycle mutation.

operations.name: reembed_clear_maintenance
operations.db3_reason: The consistency check and maintenance-marker delete must remain one DB2-owned transactional operator action.

operations.name: embedder_serving_id
operations.db3_reason: The effective vector-space identity is established during DB2 bootstrap and remains DB2 lifecycle evidence tied to the canonical corpus.

operations.name: dimension_reset
operations.db3_reason: Schema-width replacement, maintenance marking, and authoritative requeue accounting are one DB2-owned operator transaction.

operations.name: level3_count
operations.db3_reason: The global L3 count is canonical relational corpus evidence owned by DB2, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: level2_count
operations.db3_reason: The global L2 count is canonical relational corpus evidence owned by DB2, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: orphaned_l0_count
operations.db3_reason: The orphaned L0 count is canonical relational integrity evidence owned by DB2, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: total_count
operations.db3_reason: The global memory-row count is canonical relational corpus evidence owned by DB2, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: session_l2_count
operations.db3_reason: Session attribution and canonical L2 memory rows remain relational DB2 authority rather than portable ANN state.

operations.name: key_exists
operations.db3_reason: Exact canonical memory-key existence is relational DB2 authority and does not depend on portable ANN state.

operations.name: find_id_by_key_kind
operations.db3_reason: Exact canonical memory-key and kind lookup is relational DB2 authority and does not depend on portable ANN state.

operations.name: key_exists_in_tier_pair
operations.db3_reason: Exact canonical key and tier lookup is relational DB2 authority and does not depend on portable ANN state.

operations.name: effectiveness_update
operations.db3_reason: Canonical memory effectiveness is relational DB2 state derived by the host from DB1 session outcomes and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

request.consistency: has_value=0 requires value bits to be positive zero

operations.name: retention_enforce
operations.db3_reason: Canonical content-safety retention deletes relational memory rows under the fixed restricted and sensitive policies and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: effectiveness_demote
operations.db3_reason: Demoting canonical relational memory tiers from the host-defined effectiveness policy remains DB2 state management and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: effectiveness_stats
operations.db3_reason: Aggregate effectiveness over the canonical relational memory corpus is DB2 authority and does not depend on portable ANN state.

operations.name: l2_memory_ids
operations.db3_reason: Canonical L2 memory identifiers are relational DB2 authority; the host joins them against DB1 surfacing evidence, so the identifiers cross the boundary rather than the join.

operations.name: health_record
operations.db3_reason: A health-cycle snapshot row is canonical relational DB2 bookkeeping over the memory corpus and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: health_retention
operations.db3_reason: Health snapshot and contradiction retention deletes canonical relational DB2 bookkeeping rows and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: health_counters
operations.db3_reason: The rolling health-window counters aggregate canonical relational DB2 snapshot and corpus rows; the host derives its rates from them and owns no part of the aggregation.

operations.name: stats_counts
operations.db3_reason: Tier, kind, and conflict breakdowns of the canonical relational memory corpus are DB2 authority; the host layers only its own PageRank timings on top.

operations.name: expire
operations.db3_reason: Expiring canonical relational memory rows and their provenance is DB2 lifecycle authority and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: demote
operations.db3_reason: Demoting canonical relational memory tiers and cascading confidence to dependants is DB2 lifecycle authority and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: promote_stable
operations.db3_reason: Promoting settled relational memory rows into the slow-changing project tier is DB2 lifecycle authority and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: reclassify_directives
operations.db3_reason: Reclassifying canonical relational directive rows into the highest-priority tier is DB2 lifecycle authority and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: record_l4_approval
operations.db3_reason: Promotion approvals are canonical relational DB2 rows that gate a later tier change and do not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: prune_orphaned_l0
operations.db3_reason: Deleting expired orphaned L0 rows is canonical relational DB2 retention authority and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: lifecycle_sweep_expired
operations.db3_reason: Archiving canonical relational memory rows whose pending time-to-live has passed is DB2 lifecycle authority and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: demote_id
operations.db3_reason: Decaying the confidence of one canonical relational memory row is DB2 lifecycle authority and does not belong to portable ANN providers.

operations.name: has_workspace_tag
operations.db3_reason: Whether a canonical memory carries any workspace attribution is a relational DB2 join and does not depend on portable ANN state.

operations.name: delete_row
operations.db3_reason: Deleting a canonical relational memory row is DB2 authority; portable ANN providers hold derived vectors rather than the row itself.

operations.name: touch
operations.db3_reason: Use counts and last-used stamps are canonical relational retrieval evidence owned by DB2 and are not derivable from portable ANN state.

operations.name: link_delete
operations.db3_reason: Relations between canonical memories are relational DB2 rows rather than portable ANN state, so removing one stays DB2 authority.

operations.name: valid_at
operations.db3_reason: Validity bounds are canonical relational columns on the memory row and the comparison is a DB2 statement, not a portable ANN concern.

operations.name: has_scope_type
operations.db3_reason: Scope attribution rows are canonical relational DB2 joins rather than portable ANN state.

operations.name: reject
operations.db3_reason: Confidence is a canonical relational column on the memory row, so penalising it is DB2 authority rather than portable ANN state.

operations.name: update_content
operations.db3_reason: Memory content is the canonical relational column; a portable ANN provider holds only a derived vector and cannot be the authority for the text.

operations.name: decay_confidence
operations.db3_reason: Confidence is a canonical relational column on the memory row, so decaying it is DB2 authority rather than portable ANN state.

operations.name: workspace_tag_insert
operations.db3_reason: Workspace attribution rows are canonical relational DB2 joins rather than portable ANN state.

operations.name: set_cognified_kind
operations.db3_reason: The cognified kind is a canonical relational column on the memory row and is not derivable from portable ANN state.

operations.name: set_source_session
operations.db3_reason: Session attribution is a canonical relational column on the memory row and is not derivable from portable ANN state.

operations.name: negation_tokens_update
operations.db3_reason: Negation tokens are a canonical relational column on the memory row; a portable ANN provider holds a derived vector rather than the extracted tokens.

operations.name: get_content
operations.db3_reason: Memory content is the canonical relational column; a portable ANN provider holds a derived vector and cannot return the text.

operations.name: get_source_session
operations.db3_reason: Session attribution is a canonical relational column on the memory row and is not derivable from portable ANN state.

operations.name: pick_first_temporal_ref
operations.db3_reason: Temporal reference rows and their ranking are canonical relational DB2 state, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: count_and_max_updated
operations.db3_reason: The canonical memory row count and their latest update stamp are relational DB2 aggregates, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: top_l2_facts
operations.db3_reason: L2 fact rows and the scope tables they are ranked against are both relational DB2 state, so the ranking is DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then use_count, then confidence, all descending

operations.name: list_session_scope_priority
operations.db3_reason: Session-scope priority ranks canonical memory rows against DB2's own scope tables, so the ordering is DB2 authority; identifiers cross in that order and the caller reattaches content.

policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then kind (workflow, decision, other), then tier (L3, L2, other), then use_count, all descending

operations.name: collect_alias_matches
operations.db3_reason: Memory aliases are a relational DB2 table joined to the canonical rows, so alias resolution stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the alias exactly, as a prefix, or anywhere within it
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then exact alias before prefix before substring, then alias weight, then tier (L3, L2, L1, other), then use_count, then confidence

operations.name: collect_entity_matches
operations.db3_reason: Memory entities are a relational DB2 table joined to the canonical rows, so entity resolution stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the entity exactly, as a prefix, or anywhere within it
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then exact entity before prefix before substring, then entity weight, then confidence, then use_count

operations.name: collect_event_frame_matches
operations.db3_reason: Event frames are a relational DB2 table joined to the canonical rows, so frame matching stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the actor, the action, the location or the event time exactly, or the object anywhere within it
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then confidence, then use_count; which field matched does not change the order

operations.name: collect_relation_token_matches
operations.db3_reason: Memory relations are a relational DB2 table joined to the canonical rows, so relation matching stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the source entity, the destination entity or the relation exactly, or the fact text anywhere within it, all case-insensitively
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then the greatest matching relation weight, then confidence, then use_count

operations.name: collect_summary_matches
operations.db3_reason: Memory summaries are a relational DB2 table joined to the canonical rows, so summary matching stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the summary anywhere within it, case-insensitively
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then a case-insensitive prefix match before any other, then confidence, then use_count

operations.name: collect_temporal_matches
operations.db3_reason: Temporal references are a relational DB2 table joined to the canonical rows, so temporal matching stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the reference key exactly or as a prefix
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then exact reference before prefix, then reference weight, then confidence, then use_count

operations.name: find_facts_like
operations.db3_reason: Canonical memory rows and the scope tables the match is ranked against are both relational DB2 state, so the ranking is DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the key, the content or the use cases anywhere within them, case-insensitively
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then exact key, exact content, exact use cases, key prefix, anything else; then tier (L3, L2, L1, other), then use_count, then confidence

operations.name: list_session_scope_priority_like
operations.db3_reason: Session-scope priority ranks canonical memory rows against DB2's own scope tables, so the ordering is DB2 authority; identifiers cross in that order and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the key or the content against the term used as a SQL LIKE pattern, so any wildcard the caller writes is significant
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then kind (workflow, decision, other), then tier (L3, L2, other), then use_count

operations.name: negation_fts_search
operations.db3_reason: The negation text index is a relational DB2 column on the canonical rows, so the search stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the whitespace-separated negation tokens, which the handler joins with OR into one websearch_to_tsquery over the negation index
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then text-search rank, then use_count, then confidence

operations.name: session_neighbors_before
operations.db3_reason: The memories of a session and their identifier order are relational DB2 state, so walking back from an anchor stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.selects: identifiers strictly below the anchor, largest first
policy.anchor_zero: an anchor of zero selects nothing, because no identifier is below it

operations.name: session_neighbors_after
operations.db3_reason: The memories of a session and their identifier order are relational DB2 state, so walking forward from an anchor stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.selects: identifiers strictly above the anchor, smallest first
policy.anchor_zero: an anchor of zero selects the whole session from its first memory

operations.name: row_get
operations.db3_reason: The canonical memory row is relational DB2 state; this is the one place a whole row crosses, because a caller holding an identifier has nothing else to reattach it to.

policy.columns: id, tier, kind, key, content, confidence, use_count, last_used_at, created_at, updated_at, source_session, salience, provenance_category, use_cases
policy.note: a null provenance category is read back as user_stated

operations.name: row_get_by_unit_id
operations.db3_reason: Memory units and the canonical rows they point at are both relational DB2 state, so resolving a unit to its memory stays DB2 authority.

policy.columns: id, tier, kind, key, content, confidence, use_count, last_used_at, created_at, updated_at, source_session
policy.note: salience, provenance_category and use_cases are not read and come back empty

operations.name: search_facts_patterns_by_keyword
operations.db3_reason: Facts and patterns are canonical DB2 rows and the tiers and kinds that qualify are DB2 policy, so the selection stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the content or the key anywhere within them, case-insensitively, among the fact and pattern kinds in tiers L2, L3 and L5
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then confidence, then use_count

operations.name: fact_history
operations.db3_reason: A fact's versions are canonical DB2 rows keyed by a naming convention DB2 owns, so gathering them stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.matches: the key exactly, and every key the handler forms by appending the version suffix to it
policy.unbounded_statement: the statement has no LIMIT, so the database returns every version and the limit only decides how many are read back

operations.name: list_rows
operations.db3_reason: The canonical memory rows, their lifecycle state and the scope tables the listing is ranked against are all relational DB2 state, so the listing stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.empty_filter: an empty tier or kind is no filter on that column, not a match against the empty string
policy.assembled_statement: the tier and kind clauses are appended only when their value is non-empty, so this is four statements sharing one operation
policy.ranking: session-scope rank, then update stamp, both descending

operations.name: aggregate
operations.db3_reason: The canonical memory rows and the entity table the seed is matched against are both relational DB2 state, so the selection stays DB2 authority; identifiers cross and the caller reattaches content.

policy.argument_precedence: an entity seed wins outright; the keyword is only consulted when the seed is empty, and neither being set selects every kind but scratch
policy.ranking: last use, falling back to the update stamp, then identifier, both descending

operations.name: load_eval_corpus
operations.db3_reason: Which rows make an evaluation corpus, and in which order the fallbacks are tried, are DB2 policy over relational DB2 state; identifiers cross with the label of the plan that produced them.

policy.plans: L2 facts, then facts in L1 to L3, then durable memories excluding scratch; the first plan that returns a row wins
policy.plan_limit: each plan carries its own LIMIT of 100, so the request limit bounds what is read back, not what the plan selects

operations.name: record_exists
operations.db3_reason: Both tables the probe consults are relational DB2 state, so whether an identifier names anything is DB2 authority.

policy.tables: the memories table and the memory_units table; the reply does not say which one matched

operations.name: prospective_set_state
operations.db3_reason: Prospective memories and their states are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: the state is stored as given and the update stamp is DB2's own clock, so a caller records that a state changed but not when

operations.name: dedupe_by_key
operations.db3_reason: Canonical memory rows and the merge pointers between them are relational DB2 state.

policy.writes: a dry run counts what it would merge without writing, so the same count means two different things depending on the flag

operations.name: scene_member_exists
operations.db3_reason: Scenes and the memories belonging to them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the pair is matched in the order given, so membership is directional in the sense that swapping the arguments asks a different question

operations.name: unit_edge_exists
operations.db3_reason: Memory units and the edges between them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: both orders are tried, so an edge stored in either direction answers true and swapping the arguments asks the same question

operations.name: match_error_keys
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: each memory's key is used as a SQL LIKE pattern against the text, so a key containing a wildcard matches far more than its own words

operations.name: memory_ids_by_updated
operations.db3_reason: Memories and when they were last updated are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: a limit of zero means no SQL limit at all, so the wire's row bound becomes the only thing stopping the read

operations.name: unit_ids_for_memory
operations.db3_reason: Memories and the units they were split into are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the units are listed in whatever order the database returns them, because the statement has no ORDER BY

operations.name: briefing_active_entities
operations.db3_reason: Memories and the entities mentioned in them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: only memories touched in roughly the last month count, and one never touched counts because its stamp is absent rather than old

operations.name: prospective_list
operations.db3_reason: Prospective memories, their triggers and their anchors are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: an empty state lists every prospective memory rather than none, newest first

operations.name: prospective_list_armed
operations.db3_reason: Prospective memories, their triggers and their anchors are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: every armed prospective memory, with no limit in the statement, so the wire's row bound is what stops the read

operations.name: prospective_by_entity
operations.db3_reason: Prospective memories, their triggers and their anchors are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: only armed memories match, and the entity is compared lowered, so the caller has to lower it too

operations.name: prospective_by_file
operations.db3_reason: Prospective memories, their triggers and their anchors are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: only armed memories match, and the file is compared exactly, unlike the entity beside it

operations.name: prospective_by_trigger_terms
operations.db3_reason: Prospective memories, their triggers and their anchors are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the turn's words become a full-text query, so what matches depends on the English stemmer rather than on the words as written

operations.name: relations_for_entity
operations.db3_reason: The rows this reads are relational DB2 records.

policy.reads: either end of the relation may be the entity, and both are compared case-insensitively

operations.name: relations_search
operations.db3_reason: The rows this reads are relational DB2 records.

policy.reads: the query is a substring of any of four columns, so a short query matches almost everything

operations.name: relations_search_as_of
operations.db3_reason: The rows this reads are relational DB2 records.

policy.reads: a relation with no validity stamp is treated as valid at every instant, not as invalid

operations.name: relations_supporting
operations.db3_reason: The rows this reads are relational DB2 records.

policy.reads: the token is matched as a substring of either endpoint, and a relation with no fact text is skipped

operations.name: typed_fact_recall
operations.db3_reason: The rows this reads are relational DB2 records.

policy.reads: only active facts are recalled, and an empty relation drops that condition and changes the order

operations.name: global_constraints
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: preferences and policies above L0, newest first, so the constraint a caller sees first is the most recently written

operations.name: kv_section
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the section number selects one of five fixed statements, so a number outside that range reads nothing rather than failing

operations.name: memories_by_key
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the key is matched exactly and nothing orders the result, so which memories survive the bound is arbitrary

operations.name: session_memories
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: oldest first, so the limit keeps the beginning of a session rather than its most recent memories

operations.name: memory_candidates
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the filter selects one of two tier sets, and neither is a superset of the other

operations.name: recall_section
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the section number selects one of four fixed statements, and none of them reads confidence or use count

operations.name: l2_cross_key_pairs
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: every L2 memory is joined against every other and compared with a substring match, so the cost is quadratic in the tier

operations.name: l2_fact_decision_pairs
operations.db3_reason: Memories, their keys and their tiers are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: facts are joined against decisions across different tiers and compared with a substring match, so the cost is the product of the two sets

operations.name: memory_link_create
operations.db3_reason: Memories and the links between them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: the link is directional and the relation is stored unchecked, and creating one that exists does nothing and is acknowledged

operations.name: entity_edge_prune_orphans
operations.db3_reason: The entity graph and the canonical memory rows its edges are checked against are both relational DB2 state, so pruning unreferenced edges stays DB2 authority.

operations.name: entity_edge_normalize_weights
operations.db3_reason: Entity edge weights are canonical relational DB2 columns and their per-relation normalisation is a DB2 statement.

operations.name: project_count
operations.db3_reason: Indexed project rows and their lifecycle state are canonical relational DB2 records, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: purge_hidden_pollution
operations.db3_reason: Indexed file rows and their project generation are canonical relational DB2 records, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: requeue_drifted
operations.db3_reason: The ingest queue and the project generations it is driven from are canonical relational DB2 records, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: cross_repo_rebuild_routes
operations.db3_reason: Cross-repo include routes are derived relational DB2 records rebuilt from the index, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: cross_repo_rebuild_identities
operations.db3_reason: Cross-repo project identities are derived relational DB2 records rebuilt from indexed manifests, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: cross_repo_rebuild_build_deps
operations.db3_reason: Cross-repo build dependencies are derived relational DB2 records rebuilt from indexed manifests, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: drift_candidates
operations.db3_reason: Indexed file generations and their drift are canonical relational DB2 records, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: file_index_delete_project
operations.db3_reason: Project documents and their index rows are canonical relational DB2 records, not portable ANN state.

operations.name: entity_observation_count
operations.db3_reason: Entity observations are relational DB2 rows joined to canonical memories, so counting them stays DB2 authority.

policy.counts: distinct memories mentioning the entity, matched case-insensitively, so a memory naming it twice counts once

operations.name: entity_profile_fresh
operations.db3_reason: Entity profiles and their refresh stamps are relational DB2 rows, so freshness is measured against DB2's own clock.

policy.reads: the window is a Postgres interval the caller supplies, compared against DB2's clock; an unparseable one makes the statement fail rather than answer false

operations.name: project_fingerprint
operations.db3_reason: Files, their hashes and the generation they belong to are relational DB2 rows, so summarising them stays DB2 authority.

policy.reads: the fingerprint is an md5 DB2 computes over the project's current generation, so it changes when that generation does and cannot be compared across projects

operations.name: visible_source_hash
operations.db3_reason: Projection generations and their states are relational DB2 rows, so which one is visible is DB2 authority.

policy.reads: only a generation in the visible state is read, so a project whose generations are all pending reads back empty rather than reporting the newest

operations.name: entity_profile_card
operations.db3_reason: Entity profiles and the cards computed for them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the entity is matched case-insensitively, and the card crosses as the JSON document DB2 stored without being parsed or validated on the way

operations.name: generation_abort
operations.db3_reason: Projection generations and their states are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: only a pending generation is aborted, so aborting one already visible or already aborted changes nothing and is acknowledged

operations.name: generation_set_source_hash
operations.db3_reason: Projection generations and the source hashes recorded against them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: the hash is stored as given against any generation whatever its state, including one already visible

operations.name: generation_publish
operations.db3_reason: Projection generations, their states and which one a project shows are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: supersedes the project's visible generation and makes this one visible inside one transaction, so no moment has two visible generations or none

operations.name: purge_files_matching
operations.db3_reason: Indexed files and the generation they belong to are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: the pattern is bound as a SQL LIKE pattern, so a wildcard the caller writes is significant, and only the project's current generation is purged

operations.name: file_index_delete_current_generation
operations.db3_reason: The file index and the generation it belongs to are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: the project name is resolved through its aliases first, and only the current generation is deleted

operations.name: project_delete
operations.db3_reason: Projects and the files indexed under them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: the project row is deleted by its literal name and its aliases, generations and files cascade away with it

operations.name: minhash_delete_current_generation
operations.db3_reason: Minhash signatures and LSH buckets are relational DB2 rows keyed by project and generation.

policy.writes: two deletes run one after the other outside a transaction, so a failure between them leaves signatures gone and their buckets behind

operations.name: minhash_delete_file
operations.db3_reason: Minhash signatures are relational DB2 rows keyed by project, generation and file.

policy.writes: only the signature is deleted, so the LSH buckets built from it are left behind

operations.name: project_current_generation
operations.db3_reason: Projects and the generation they are on are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: only a project in the current lifecycle state answers, and zero comes back for one that is not, one that does not exist, and one whose generation really is zero

operations.name: projection_generation_create
operations.db3_reason: Projection generations and the projects they belong to are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: the extractor and pipeline versions written are the build version of whichever process runs the statement, which over the bus is the module's and not the caller's

operations.name: projection_visible_id
operations.db3_reason: Projection generations and their visibility are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: both the generation and the project it names must be current, so a visible generation on a retired project reads back as none

operations.name: unique_file_basename
operations.db3_reason: Indexed files and the generation they belong to are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: every path in the project's current generation is read and the basename compared in the module, and a path is returned only when exactly one file matches

operations.name: entity_neighbors
operations.db3_reason: Entity edges, their endpoints and weights are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: edges are followed in both directions and returned unordered, so which neighbours survive the limit is arbitrary

operations.name: entity_neighbors_filtered
operations.db3_reason: Entity edges, their relations and weights are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: an empty second relation narrows to one, a limit of zero becomes twenty, and without the weight ordering the surviving rows are arbitrary

operations.name: entity_outbound_neighbors
operations.db3_reason: Entity edges, their endpoints and weights are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: only edges leaving the entity are followed, which is the opposite of the neighbour listing beside it

operations.name: entity_top_partners
operations.db3_reason: Entity edges, their relations and weights are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: endpoints are matched case-insensitively and the weights of both directions are summed per partner

operations.name: entity_top_targets
operations.db3_reason: Entity edges, their relations and weights are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: only edges leaving the entity are summed, and the endpoint is matched case-insensitively

operations.name: file_definitions
operations.db3_reason: Indexed files and the terms extracted from them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the file must be in the project's current generation, and a line_end of zero means the symbol's extent was never recorded

operations.name: code_search

operations.db3_reason: The synthesis queue and the failure text on its rows are relational DB2 state.

policy.writes: the attempt counter is incremented by the statement, so a caller cannot set it or read it back

operations.name: runtime_state_set
operations.db3_reason: Runtime state keys and values are relational DB2 bookkeeping.

policy.writes: an existing key is overwritten rather than refused, so this sets rather than creates

operations.name: set_active_embedder_version
operations.db3_reason: The active embedder version is relational DB2 state governing DB2's own vector rows.

policy.writes: the stamp is the caller's, and the row is a single fixed row that is overwritten

operations.name: runtime_state_get
operations.db3_reason: Runtime state keys and values are relational DB2 bookkeeping, so reading one back is DB2 authority.

policy.reads: a key that is not set reads back as the empty value, so a caller cannot tell an unset key from one set to nothing

operations.name: ingest_queue_fail
operations.db3_reason: The ingest queue and the failure text on its rows are relational DB2 state.

policy.writes: the completion stamp is DB2's own clock, and a job already in another state is moved to failed regardless of what it was

operations.name: reset_stuck_vector_ops
operations.db3_reason: Both vector operation queues are relational DB2 state governing DB2's own vector rows.

policy.writes: resets two queues and reports their totals added together, so a caller cannot tell which queue the rows came from, and a failure in one is hidden by the other's count

operations.name: directive_resolve
operations.db3_reason: Epistemic directives, their states and the memories that resolve them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: only an open directive is resolved, and the memory that resolves it is recorded without being checked to exist

operations.name: css_migration_enumerate
operations.db3_reason: CSS migration units and the component files they are derived from are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: at most 4096 component files are read, and each one is upserted as a migration unit without a transaction around the set

operations.name: css_migration_assert_conventions
operations.db3_reason: CSS rules, declarations and the typed facts derived from them are relational DB2 rows.

policy.writes: two configuration flags are read inside the module, and the timestamp written is the one the caller supplied rather than DB2's own clock

operations.name: css_migration_rules_doc
operations.db3_reason: CSS rules and declarations are relational DB2 rows; the document is derived from them.

policy.reads: the document is a fixed template with three derived numbers in it, so it is written even for a project with nothing indexed

operations.name: retryable_index_failures
operations.db3_reason: Vector index operations and their attempt counts are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: the oldest failures come first and a limit of zero means no SQL limit, so the wire's row bound is what stops the read

operations.name: active_embedder_version
operations.db3_reason: The active embedder version is a relational DB2 record, not portable vector state.

policy.reads: one row holds the answer, so an empty version means no embedder has been made active rather than that this caller cannot see one

operations.name: corpus_pipeline_stage_counts
operations.db3_reason: Corpus processing jobs and the stages they are in are relational DB2 rows.

policy.reads: one row per stage and status that has at least one job, so a stage with no jobs is absent rather than zero

operations.name: directive_list

operations.name: directive_by_entity

operations.name: directive_by_file

operations.name: directive_by_lexical

operations.name: memory_lint
operations.db3_reason: The rows this reads are relational DB2 records.

operations.name: decision_log_list

operations.name: decision_log_list_scoped

operations.name: decision_log_active_id

policy.writes: the old snapshot is deleted before the new one is inserted, without a transaction, so a failure between them leaves no snapshot at all
